question.:question/problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the curve defined parametrically by

$$
(\frac{x - 6}{4})=\frac{1}{t-2},\,\,\,y={t}^{2},\,t\ne 2.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the Cartesian equation, we eliminate $t.$ First, we use the $(\frac{x - 6}{4})$ equation to solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(\frac{x - 6}{4}) & =\frac{1}{t-2} \\ (\frac{x - 6}{4})(t-2) & =1 \\ t-2 & =\frac{1}{(\frac{x - 6}{4})} \\ t & =\frac{1}{(\frac{x - 6}{4})}+2 \\ t & =\frac{1+2(\frac{x - 6}{4})}{(\frac{x - 6}{4})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now substituting $t=\frac{1+2(\frac{x - 6}{4})}{(\frac{x - 6}{4})}$ into our expression for $y={t}^{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={(\frac{1+2(\frac{x - 6}{4})}{(\frac{x - 6}{4})})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So the Cartesian equation of the given curve is $y={(\frac{1+2(\frac{x - 6}{4})}{(\frac{x - 6}{4})})}^{2}.$

Finally, since $t\ne 2$ and $(\frac{x - 6}{4})=\frac{1}{t-2},$ we must have $(\frac{x - 6}{4})\ne 0.$

So, the complete Cartesian equation is

$$
y={(\frac{1+2(\frac{x - 6}{4})}{(\frac{x - 6}{4})})}^{2},\,(\frac{x - 6}{4})\ne 0.
$$
